status_summary: On 2025-09-19 HHS announced a safety review of the mifepristone REMS (the 2023 REMS allows telehealth prescribing and mail or retail pharmacy dispensing), and on 2025-09-30 FDA approved an additional generic mifepristone under the same REMS. As of 2026-10-13 no completed review, REMS change or label change was found, and FDA's page documenting the REMS was last updated 2025-01-17. In a court-ordered status report filed 2026-10-07 in the Louisiana case, FDA said, according to Associated Press reporting, that its safety study should be complete by mid-December 2026 and a report on the findings is expected no later than March 2027, after which it will decide whether to impose new restrictions or other changes; the filing itself was not read. Courts have deferred to the review: the Western District of Louisiana paused Louisiana v. FDA for six months in April 2026, and a Texas federal court paused Texas and Florida's suit against the 2000 approval until 2026-12-01 or completion of the review (reported 2026-09-01). A Fifth Circuit order of 2026-05-01 reinstating in-person dispensing nationwide was blocked by the Supreme Court on 2026-05-14 (two justices dissenting); the Fifth Circuit heard argument on Louisiana's appeal on 2026-09-09 (No. 26-30203) and no ruling was found. The FDA Commissioner nominee told the Senate HELP Committee on 2026-09-24 that FDA has found the drug safe and effective with its risk mitigation requirements.

timeline.event: HHS Secretary announces a review of the mifepristone REMS, launched through a September 2025 letter from the Secretary and the FDA Commissioner to Republican state attorneys general.

FDA approves an additional generic mifepristone under the same REMS (a second generic sponsor; the approval is not a withdrawal or tightening, and runs against the Mandate's call to stop approving mail-order distribution).

Louisiana sues FDA over the 2023 REMS (October 2025; exact day not given, first of month used). In the same month a federal court in Hawaii (Purcell v. Kennedy; the order is labeled 2025-10-30 in a link KFF cites) finds FDA did not give a reasoned explanation for keeping certain restrictions in 2023 and orders review of overlooked evidence.

In Louisiana v. FDA, which the Western District of Louisiana had paused for six months earlier in April so FDA could continue its review, the Justice Department files a brief describing a REMS review that includes a new study and is expected to take under a year from September 2025; a status report on the review is due 2026-10-07 (per the Center for Reproductive Rights; the brief itself was not read).

The Supreme Court blocks the Fifth Circuit's 2026-05-01 order (which had reinstated in-person dispensing nationwide pending appeal), Justices Alito and Thomas dissenting; the 2023 REMS stays in effect while the case returns to the Fifth Circuit.

A report dated 2026-09-01 says the Northern District of Texas (Judge Reed O'Connor) paused the Texas and Florida suit seeking to revoke the 2000 mifepristone approval, at the Justice Department's request and with the states' agreement, until 2026-12-01 or completion of FDA's safety review, whichever comes first; the report says an administration official stated in June that the review would likely take about six months.

A three-judge Fifth Circuit panel hears argument in Louisiana v. FDA (No. 26-30203) on Louisiana's request to stay the 2023 REMS changes; the panel raised whether it can reimpose a stay the Supreme Court blocked and whether Louisiana has standing, and gave no ruling date. A Justice Department lawyer argued Louisiana lacks standing.

At her Senate HELP Committee confirmation hearing as FDA Commissioner nominee (the prior Commissioner left in May), Heidi Overton says FDA has found mifepristone safe and effective with its risk mitigation requirements, would not say whether she agrees or predict the outcome of FDA's internal review, and the committee has not yet voted.

FDA files a court-ordered status report in Louisiana v. FDA; per AP reporting, it says the mifepristone safety study should be complete by mid-December 2026, a report is due no later than March 2027, and the agency will then decide whether to change restrictions; FDA is also weighing citizen petitions on prescribing and distribution.

title: Restore in-person dispensing and stricter FDA rules for mifepristone, or withdraw approval
uncertainties: No FDA or HHS primary document announcing the review or the generic approval could be reached (the FDA mifepristone page was last updated 2025-01-17); the September 2025 dates come from KFF, and an earlier review noted a Wikipedia entry placing the generic approval in October 2025, a few days later than KFF's 2025-09-30. A Federal Register query for 'mifepristone' found no FDA REMS action through 2026-10-13. FDA's 2026-10-07 status report is known only from an Associated Press report (via ksat.com) and the filing itself was not read; the report also says FDA is weighing several citizen petitions on prescribing and distribution. The April 2026 DOJ brief is described through a Center for Reproductive Rights summary (an advocacy source) and was not read; the Texas and Florida pause comes from a syndicated report whose order date is inferred; the Fifth Circuit argument is from Bloomberg Law and the nominee's remarks from Fierce Pharma, both read through summarizing fetches. No Fifth Circuit ruling was found as of the AP report. Source dates for the CRR, NewsChannel 9, Bloomberg Law and Fierce items are the filing, report or event dates. The Mandate text on p. 458 is read as restoring in-person dispensing, consistent with p. 459. Month-only events use the first of the month. Stage proposed (12) rests on a review that is announced and underway but has produced no operative change; match is partial because the review does not itself track the specific restrictions the Mandate lists.
